50.original: (-Grizzled Passenger-)You were moanin' somethin' fierce for a while there.

51.original: (-Grizzled Passenger-)Feelin' the effects of the aether, I reckon.

52.original: (-Grizzled Passenger-)You'll get used to it, though, don't worry.

56.original: (-Grizzled Passenger-)I'm just an honest peddler, friend. So, er...don't be too disappointed if you don't find nothin', eh?

57.original: Mind your tongue, old man, lest I cut it out!

59.original: Honest peddler, was it? Since when do honest peddlers deal in prohibited herbs?

60.original: You're in a lot of trouble, old man. You'll rot in a dungeon till the end of your days...unless you can afford the fine.

63.original: Amalj'aa! Amalj'aa! To arms! To arms!

64.original: Seven hells... Consider this a warning! Now <hex:021A020203>go<hex:021A020103>─all of you!

65.original: (-Grizzled Passenger-)Phew... That kind of excitement ain't good for the heart.

66.original: (-Grizzled Passenger-)You be careful 'round them Brass Blades, <hex:02080EE905FF056C617373FF046C616403>. Bastards'll have the shirt off your back if they fancy it. Like common bandits, they are, only less honest.

67.original: (-Grizzled Passenger-)Thank the gods for sendin' some beastmen to the rescue, eh!?

68.original: (-Grizzled Passenger-)Hey, seein' as we've still got a long ride ahead, you mind keepin' me company till we arrive?

69.original: (-Grizzled Passenger-)Them young'uns don't much care for conversation, see.

70.original: Brendt's the name, an' peddlin's me trade.

71.original: An' judgin' by your unusual garments, I'll wager you're one of them new adventurers.

72.original: I knew it! Goin' wherever the wind blows, seekin' fortune an' glory─now <hex:021A020203>that's<hex:021A020103> what I call livin'!

73.original: So long as you can avoid dyin', I mean. Ain't no secret that adventurin's a risky business─these days especially.

74.original: What was it that first attracted you to it?

75.original: Why did you become an adventurer?

80.original: ...<hex:021A020203>Power<hex:021A020103>? As in, er...power to do good? Like protectin' the weak, an' fightin' for what's right, an' all that? Aye, I thought that's what you meant. Well, adventurers do get up to a lot of fightin', that's for sure. You'll never be short of a chance to polish your warcraft in the adventurin' business.

81.original: When you arrive in town, you'd best enroll at the Adventurers' Guild─they'll set you on the right path.

82.original: An' it wouldn't hurt to join a guild, neither.

83.original: Ul'dah's home to a few, so if you fancy learnin' how to fight with a sword, your fists, or even spells, you should think about seekin' one out.

84.original: Glory, eh? Well, if you're willin' to take on them tasks as other folk ain't, an adventurer such as yourself can win fame what coin can't buy.

85.original: When you arrive in town, you'll want to report to the Adventurers' Guild.

86.original: You can find out everythin' you need to know about the adventurin' business in there.

87.original: Fortune, eh? Heh heh! Then I reckon you'll fit right in where we're goin'!

88.original: Once you've learned to handle yourself in a fight, you'll want to pay a visit to whichever craftin' or gatherin' guild tickles your fancy.

89.original: An' there're plenty to choose from, too. Whether it be weavin', alchemy, goldsmithin', or minin' that interests you, Ul'dah's got a place where you can learn your trade.

90.original: Adventurin' ain't just about killin' things, after all. A peaceful pastime may well help you make your fortune!

91.original: Well, if you ain't inclined to tell, I ain't about to pry. Might be as ol' Brendt's a chatterbox, but he sure as hells ain't no busybody.

92.original: We all have a secret or three, don't we? Me? <hex:021A020203>Dozens<hex:021A020103>.

93.original: An' I'd rather they stayed secret, too─which is why I don't go stickin' me nose where it ain't welcome.

94.original: Just remember, though: there're more important things than fortune an' glory. Such as <hex:021A020203>breathin'<hex:021A020103>. Ain't no profit in bein' dead, an' that's a fact.

95.original: By the by, is this your first trip to Ul'dah?

96.original: Is this your first trip to Ul'dah?

99.original: It is!? Well then, let this journeyed itinerant tell you the ins an' outs of your destination.

100.original: But of course it ain't! Still, might be as this journeyed itinerant has a few new things to teach you about your destination. Ahem!

101.original: Ul'dah's ruled by the sultana in name, but as most folk know, the Syndicate holds all the real power.

102.original: Them and their Monetarist cronies would happily get rid of Her Grace altogether, but that won't happen while she still commands the loyalty of the Royalists─an' the Royalists are nothin' if not loyal.

103.original: These factions have long fought over power, throwin' the weight of their wealth against each other, an' they show no sign of stoppin'.

104.original: 'Course the lizardmen─that's the <hex:021A020203>Amalj'aa<hex:021A020103>─couldn't care less about Ul'dahn politics. They have their own interests, see─an' they ain't afraid to use force to serve 'em.

105.original: They say war is a gift to peddlers─need breedin' profit─an' though it shames me to say it, I'm inclined to agree...

107.original: Behold Ul'dah, jewel of Thanalan, where folk turn sand into gold!

108.original: Deep in the sunbaked south, surrounded by the shifting sands of an endless desert, she rises.

109.original: A solitary rose amidst the dust and rock. A symbol of defiance. Her name: Ul'dah.

110.original: Even with the coming of the Seventh Umbral Era,<hex:02100103>hope springs eternal for the mongers and merchants who vie for lost fortunes in this bustling oasis.

111.original: As the Twin Faces of Nald'thal maintain Their vigil over all<hex:02100103>that has been and shall be, the present proffers a brave soul...

112.original: ...One whose arrival could mark the beginning of a new era of prosperity for the realm.

113.original: An' here's where we part ways, <hex:02080EE905FF056C617373FF046C616403>.

114.original: I'm off to the markets to deliver me wares, then it's on to the highroad for me.

115.original: Here, I want you to have this─by way of thanks for puttin' up with me prattle.

116.original: You never did tell me your name, though. Hey, but here's an idea...

117.original: Become the sort of storied personage I can brag about havin' met, an' I'll consider us square.

118.original: May the Traders nurture our fortunes as They kindle the flames which burn within us all.

119.original: For by fire are we reborn.

122.original: (-???-)Fresh off the carriage, by any chance? Eh? How can I tell? Heh!

123.original: Name's Wymond, an' my business is knowin' every bugger else's!

124.original: Now then, what if I was to offer you some invaluable advice by way of welcome to our fair city? Free of charge, even─just this once, like.
